# Zekke

> Zekke is a zero-knowledge personal drive for passwords, seed phrases, notes, documents, spreadsheets and files. Everything is encrypted on the user's device before it is sent, with keys that only the user holds. Zekke's servers hold no key that opens any of it. The recovery phrase is the account: there is no email, no password, and no account recovery of any kind.

Zekke is the commercial name of Cryple LLC (Sheridan, Wyoming, USA). The website is available in English, Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese.

## What it stores

- Secrets: seed phrases, keys and account numbers, hidden until the user asks for them
- Passwords: sites, usernames and passwords, saved and filled by the browser extension
- Notes: short text for quick thoughts and private details, kept in tabs
- Documents: long-form rich text that syncs across devices as you type, encrypted end to end; the server stores and forwards sealed changes and merges nothing
- Spreadsheets: encrypted, synced across devices
- Drive: any file, in folders, with a Trash
- Safe sharing: send an item or file to another Zekke user; the server relays a blob it cannot open

## How it works

1. The browser generates a 12- or 24-word BIP39 recovery phrase on the user's device. The account address and the root keys are derived from it locally. Nothing is sent. The phrase itself is never stored on a device.
2. Every item gets its own random key, generated on the device. It is wrapped under a random key for that kind of data, and that key is wrapped to the recovery phrase and to each device that holds it.
3. The server receives a sealed blob plus what routing needs: its size and when it changed. It also sees how many devices an account has and who is connected to whom. There is no master key, no recovery database and no support tool that can open a vault.
4. Typing the phrase into a new browser enrols it as a device and restores the whole vault. Each device has its own keys and its own 6-digit device PIN, which unlocks them.

## Security model

- Zero-knowledge by construction, not by policy: Zekke cannot read user data, even under legal compulsion, because it never holds a key that could decrypt it. Zekke does not claim anonymity: it can see that items exist, roughly how large they are, and when they changed.
- Losing the recovery phrase means losing the vault. Nobody, including Zekke, can restore access. Users verify their copy of the phrase at sign-up and receive a printable recovery kit. A lost device is different: it can be removed from another device or with the phrase, and the keys it held are rotated.
- Standard mode (recommended, the default): the recovery phrase alone protects the account, and each device has its own 6-digit device PIN. The server counts every guess through an OPRF without ever seeing the PIN. After ten wrong tries that device forgets the account until the phrase is typed again. Users can upgrade to Paranoid at any time from Settings.
- Paranoid mode (two factors): a recovery phrase plus a 6-digit account PIN. Adding a device with the phrase, removing devices and deleting the account all need the account PIN, so a stolen phrase cannot do any of them. Paranoid cannot be turned off, and a forgotten account PIN ends the account.
- Post-quantum: data at rest uses AES-256-GCM, which is considered resistant to known quantum attacks. Sharing between accounts uses PQXDH, a hybrid of X25519 and ML-KEM-768, so an attacker must break both a classical and a post-quantum algorithm.

## Technical specifications

- Symmetric encryption: AES-256-GCM
- Classic key exchange: X25519 (ECDH)
- Post-quantum KEM: ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203), for sharing
- Hybrid protocol: PQXDH (X25519 + ML-KEM-768), for sharing
- Key derivation: BIP39 (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 2048 iterations) → SLIP-0010 P-256
- Authentication: ECDSA P-256 signature over a fresh, timestamped, single-use challenge; no secret is transmitted
- PIN rationing: OPRF (RFC 9497, ristretto255-SHA512); the server counts guesses and never sees either PIN
- PIN derivation: Argon2id (64 MiB, t=3, p=1), client-side

## Business model and pricing

- No ads, no tracking, no cookies.
- A free tier with 500 MB of storage; paid plans add storage. Final prices are not published yet.
- Waitlist members get 50% off premium subscriptions during the first month after launch.

## Release status

- September 2026: staging, live now at https://test-app.zekke.io. Secrets, passwords, notes, documents, spreadsheets, Drive and safe sharing all work today, in Standard and Paranoid mode. A free account has 500 MB of encrypted storage.
- Next: Calendar and To-do, a public inbox link anyone can use to send files without an account, a Gallery for photos and videos, and a space for official papers like a passport and contracts.
- 2027: production launch; no date yet.
